newsitem.title: INDIA: India relaxes norms for foreign investment in debt.
newsitem.headline: India relaxes norms for foreign investment in debt.

text.p: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) will be allowed to invest their entire portfolio in Indian debt instruments against the existing cap of 30 percent, the Economic Times daily reported on Sunday.
This could be done either through dedicated debt funds or as sub-accounts of existing funds.
The paper quoted guidelines issued by Indian market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
Such investments would be allowed only in debt securities of companies which are already listed or likely to be listed soon the paper quoted SEBI as saying.
At present FIIs are allowed to invest a maximum of 30 percent of their funds in debt and the rest in equity.
FIIs registered with SEBI could approach it for specific approval as a separate category of FII investing purely in debt or as a sub-account of the existing entity, the paper said.
Where such approval is not sought, the existing ceiling of 30 percent on investment in debt would continue to apply, it said.

The paper said FIIs choosing the 100 percent debt route could invest in securities without any restriction on maturity. There would also be no restrictions on the size of investment in the securities issued by any individual company.

The Economic Times said SEBI would impose ceilings on individual funds or sub-accounts based on the track record of the FII and its experience in managing debt funds in emerging markets and other objective criteria.
The overall ceiling for FII investment in Indian debt would be between $one billion and $1.5 billions.
